source_candidate.candidate_scope: OCI Distribution content-addressed blob retrieval as a passive global lookup route from Git commit SHA-1 573f2f0a00718109e2cd2fc1c1c9bf2f5a0404de

verified_points: The specification defines a Repository as a scope for API calls on a Registry.
A blob is addressable by a digest, but pulling or checking a blob uses /v2/<name>/blobs/<digest> where <name> is the repository namespace.
Therefore the digest alone is not the complete OCI Distribution lookup coordinate: a registry endpoint and repository namespace are also required.
Git traditionally names an object by SHA-1 over its type, length, NUL byte, and SHA-1-form object content.
Git's SHA-256 transition uses a distinct SHA-256 object representation and stores a bidirectional SHA-1/SHA-256 mapping locally.

For commit and tree objects, SHA-1-form and SHA-256-form content differ because referenced object names differ; the alternate object name is obtained via object data/mapping rather than generically from the SHA-1 string alone.

verified_claims.claim: OCI Distribution content addressing is repository-namespace scoped, so a Git commit hash by itself does not identify a global OCI blob location.
verified_claims.reason: The normative blob endpoint requires <name> and <digest> at a chosen registry endpoint.

verified_claims.claim: A traditional Git commit SHA-1 does not by itself determine an OCI content digest for independently pre-existing content.
verified_claims.reason: Git's alternate SHA-256 object name depends on the object representation/mapping; the SHA-1 object name string is not a generic conversion key to another CAS digest.

verified_claims.claim: OCI Distribution can provide content-integrity verification once registry, repository namespace and compatible digest are already known, but it does not satisfy the tested namespace-free global passive discovery requirement.
verified_claims.reason: The spec supports digest-addressed retrieval and response-body verification inside a specified repository, not global provider/repository discovery from digest alone.

scope_limits: This audit verifies the specification-level namespace and digest semantics only.
It does not test any particular public registry's residency, anonymous-access policy, rate limits, quotas or pricing.
It does not prove that no higher-level external index could map a Git commit hash to an OCI registry/repository; such an index would be a separate dependency outside this tested candidate.
It does not prove full scheduled-Chat parity, zero finite quota dependency for any deployed provider, or zero incremental cost beyond this passive primary-source audit.

phase1_assessment.reason: Primary sources support the narrow falsification: OCI CAS integrity is useful only after registry/repository/digest coordinates are known; the end-to-end provider/location-discovery and zero-quota/zero-cost acceptance gates remain unresolved.
